prompt: A request fails after passing through three services. Which pillar is specifically designed to show which service in that chain caused the failure, by following one request's causal path across all three?
choices: Metrics
Logs
Traces
Dashboards

prompt: Which pillar is cheap enough to evaluate every 15-30 seconds across an entire fleet, which is exactly why it's the pillar you alert on?
choices: Logs
Traces
Metrics
Dashboards

prompt: What does the PromQL expression rate(http_requests_total[5m]) compute?
choices: The total number of requests received in the last 5 minutes
The per-second average rate of increase of the counter over the trailing 5-minute window
The instantaneous requests-per-second at the exact current moment
The difference between the current value and the single previous scrape

prompt: Why is `http_requests_total{status="500"} > 0` a broken alert expression?
choices: Because Prometheus counters only increase, so once a single 500 is ever recorded the expression stays true essentially forever, firing continuously
Because counters reset to zero on every scrape, so the expression is never true
Because label matchers like status="500" are invalid PromQL syntax
Because the `>` comparison operator cannot be used with counter metrics

prompt: In an alert rule, what does `for: 10m` do?
choices: It delays running the query by 10 minutes after the rule is loaded
It requires the alert expression to evaluate true continuously for 10 minutes before the alert actually fires, filtering out brief spikes
It automatically re-fires the alert every 10 minutes once it is active
It sets how long Prometheus retains the alert's historical data

prompt: In OpenTelemetry, what is a span?
choices: A single aggregated numeric time series sampled at fixed intervals
A raw, unstructured text log line written to stdout
A timed unit of work, with a start/end time, attributes, and a parent/child relationship to other spans, that becomes one segment of a trace
A saved Grafana dashboard panel definition

prompt: What does histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) tell you?
choices: The total number of requests observed in the last 5 minutes
The p95 latency: 95% of requests in the trailing window completed faster than this value
The mean (average) latency across all requests ever recorded
The single slowest request latency ever recorded for this service

prompt: A naive alert fires the instant CPU usage crosses 80%, with no sustained-duration requirement. Why does this specifically cause alert fatigue?
choices: It pages on-call for brief, harmless spikes with no duration check, so people get paged for noise and start ignoring or muting the alert entirely
It can never fire because CPU usage never reaches 80% in practice
It requires manual acknowledgement from every on-call engineer before it can be dismissed
Prometheus cannot query CPU usage metrics, so the rule silently fails
